0.name: Population
0.description: Residents per km² of land. Each municipality's population (INE Padrón, 2025) is shared among its hexes in proportion to the part of the municipality each one covers. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

1.name: Income
1.description: Mean net income per person of each hex's municipalities, weighted by population (INE Household Income Distribution Atlas, 2024: tax records matched to the Padrón). It is a mean per person, not the US map's median per household. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

2.name: Poverty
2.unit: population below 60% of the median income
2.description: Share of residents whose income per consumption unit is below 60% of the national median, the EU at-risk-of-poverty threshold (INE Household Income Distribution Atlas, 2024: income from tax records, modified OECD scale). It is a threshold relative to Spain's income, not the US map's fixed poverty line. Population-weighted in hexes with several municipalities. Small municipalities may have no figure (statistical confidentiality) and do not count in their hex. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

3.name: Mean age
3.description: Mean age of the residents of each hex's municipalities, weighted by population (demographic indicators of the INE Household Income Distribution Atlas, 2024, drawn from the Annual Population Census). It is the mean: INE publishes no median age by municipality, which is what the US map shows. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

4.name: Born abroad
4.description: Share of residents born outside Spain (INE Annual Population Census, table 65031, 1 January 2026), population-weighted in hexes with several municipalities. It counts the place of birth, not nationality: a Spaniard born abroad counts; a foreigner born in Spain does not. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

5.name: Higher education
5.description: Share of residents aged 15 or over whose highest completed level of education is higher education: university degrees and higher vocational training (INE Annual Population Census, table 66592, 1 January 2024), weighted by population. The US map counts adults aged 25 or over with a bachelor's degree; INE gives age only for municipalities of 500 residents or more, so here everyone from 15 is counted and the share comes out lower. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

6.name: Homeowners
6.description: Share of main dwellings (a household's usual residence) that are owned, against renting and other forms of tenure such as rent-free use (INE Population and Housing Census, 1 January 2021: indicators by census section added up by municipality), weighted by population. The smallest municipalities have no figure: INE does not publish their sections (statistical confidentiality). Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

7.name: Home value
7.description: Mean value per built m² of free-market housing from the appraisals of Q2 2026 (appraised value statistic of the Ministerio de Vivienda; Spain: 2,355 €/m²). The figure is the province's, because the series by municipality cannot be downloaded: a hex carries its province's, or the population-weighted mean if it touches two. It is a price per m², not the US map's median value of a whole home. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

8.name: Heritage
8.description: Bienes de Interés Cultural (Spain's highest heritage protection: monuments, sites, historic ensembles) in each hex, as Wikidata places them. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

9.name: Museums
9.description: Museums in each hex: the 2,517 museums, galleries, science museums and interpretation centres of Spain that Wikidata places. Hover a hex to see their names. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

10.name: Designations of origin
10.description: How many of the 398 names Spain has in the EU register (eAmbrosia: PDO, PGI, wines and spirit drinks) include each hex in their area. 290 areas are those of the Ministry of Agriculture (2017 revision). For 94 the Ministry has not mapped (nearly all the PGI wines and the names registered since 2017) the area is the one their specification or EU single document delimits, drawn on the IGN's municipal boundaries; the tooltip says so after the kind: “community”, “province”, “island” or “municipalities” (a municipality only partly inside counts whole). The 14 single-estate wines without a Ministry area are an estate: they go on one hex, that of their municipality's centre (“estate”). Each hex lists the smallest areas first. Left off the map as no longer registered: Aceite de la Comunitat Valenciana (PDO), Carne Morucha de Salamanca (PGI). Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

11.name: Regional dishes
11.unit: dishes and products of the province
11.description: The 577 dishes, cured meats, cheeses, sweets, breads and wines that the Spanish Wikipedia lists under each province's cuisine (and that Wikidata classes as food or drink). Hover a hex to see its province's. Volunteer-edited: some provinces are far better covered than others. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

12.name: Pre-Roman peoples
12.description: The ancient people whose location in Pleiades is nearest each hex (up to 175 km): Vaccaei, Vascones, Cantabri, Ilergetes… and, in the south and east, the regions named after their peoples (Turdetania, Bastetania, Contestania). The borders are nearest-point territories drawn by this map: Pleiades gives each people a point, not a boundary. The names are in Latin or Greek, as in Pleiades.

13.name: Languages
13.description: Where each language is official, municipality by municipality, according to the law: co-official in all of Catalonia, the Balearic Islands, Galicia and the Basque Country; Aranese in the Val d'Aran; the Basque-speaking and mixed areas of Navarre (Ley Foral 18/1986); in the Valencian Community, the Spanish-speaking municipalities of Llei 4/1983 (where Valencian is co-official too); Asturian, protected but not co-official. Aragonese and the Catalan of Aragon have no published list of municipalities yet, so Aragon shows Spanish only. Dialects (Andalusian, Canarian…) are not legal categories and are not mapped.

14.name: Blue Flag
14.description: The 677 Blue Flag beaches of 2026-27, named on hover. ADEAC gives each beach's municipality, not its position, so a municipality's beaches are shared among its coastal hexes.

15.name: Tourist dwellings
15.description: Dwellings let to tourists per 1,000 inhabitants: the 341,001 that INE finds advertised on the large platforms and matches to the Cadastre (experimental statistic, 05/2026), over the Padrón residents (2025). In a hex, the population-weighted mean of its municipalities. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

16.name: Fiestas of tourist interest
16.description: The 90 Fiestas of International Tourist Interest and the 164 of National Tourist Interest declared by the Secretaría de Estado de Turismo (Sanfermines, Fallas, the Tomatina, El Rocío, Holy Week in Seville…), each on the hex of its municipality's capital; a route or a valley, on those of all its municipalities, once per hex. A fiesta promoted to International counts once. Hover a hex to see their names.

17.name: Bars
17.description: Bars and pubs in OpenStreetMap (amenity=bar and amenity=pub, 42,122 in Spain; no cafés or restaurants) per 1,000 Padrón inhabitants, counted in their municipality. In a hex, the population-weighted mean of its municipalities. Volunteers map them and coverage is very uneven: cities and tourist coasts are far better mapped than villages, where a zero can be an unmapped bar. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

18.name: Party index
18.description: This map's own index, not an official statistic: how many times Spain's usual a hex has in bars, tourist dwellings and fiestas of tourist interest, as the geometric mean of three factors. Bars and tourist dwellings: their number per inhabitant ÷ Spain's, counting each hex with 1,000 more residents at Spain's rate, so a hamlet with one bar does not pass for Benidorm. Fiestas: 1 + their points (International 2, National 1). 1 is the usual; everything up to it stays dark.

19.name: Castles
19.description: The 3,009 castles of Spain that Wikidata places (alcazabas, alcázares, tower houses and ruined castles included; demolished ones left out). Hover a hex to see their names. Volunteer-edited: the coverage is not that of an official inventory. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

20.name: Bullrings
20.description: The 650 bullrings of Spain that Wikidata places (of any category; demolished ones left out). Hover a hex to see their names. Volunteer-edited: the coverage is not that of the official register.

21.name: Forest
21.description: Share of the hex's land covered by broadleaved, coniferous or mixed forest (CORINE 311–313). Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

22.name: Farmland
22.description: Share of the hex's land in crops, meadows or dehesas (CORINE 2xx, matched to NLCD classes 81 and 82). Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

23.name: Built-up
23.description: Share of the hex's land that is built up: urban fabric, industrial and commercial areas, transport networks, ports, airports and construction sites (CORINE 111, 112, 121–124 and 133; urban green and sports areas are not counted). Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

24.name: Broadband
24.unit: households covered at 100 Mbps or more
24.description: Share of each municipality's households that a fixed or fixed-wireless network of 100 Mbps or more reaches under peak demand (coverage report of the Ministerio para la Transformación Digital, June 2025, from the operators' data by cadastral parcel; Spain: 97.9%). It is coverage, not subscriptions: the US map counts subscribing households. A hex shows the population-weighted mean of its municipalities. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

25.name: Work elsewhere
25.unit: employed who work in another municipality
25.description: Share of employed residents who work in a municipality other than their own (in their province, in another province of their autonomous community or in another community), among those whose place of work is known (INE Annual Population Census, 1 January 2024; Spain: 57.3%). The 151 municipalities INE publishes (provincial capitals and main cities) have their own figure; the others take the rest of their province's (the province minus those municipalities). INE does not publish commuting time by municipality: this is where people work, not the US map's minutes to work. A hex shows the population-weighted mean of its municipalities. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

26.name: Life expectancy
26.description: Life expectancy at birth, both sexes, in 2024 (INE Basic Demographic Indicators). The 155 municipalities INE calculates it for have their own; the others take their province's, which includes those municipalities (a life expectancy cannot be subtracted). It takes the place of the US map's wellbeing index (CDC health estimates). A hex shows the population-weighted mean of its municipalities. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

27.name: Religious weddings
27.note: Spain has no census of religion: this measures how people marry, not what they believe.
27.description: Share of the marriages of 2025 celebrated by a religious denomination (INE does not separate Catholic from other weddings in these tables), by the couple's place of residence (INE Marriage Statistics; Spain: 16.1%). The 150 municipalities INE publishes (provincial capitals and main cities) have their own figure; the others take the rest of their province's (the province minus those municipalities). A hex shows the population-weighted mean of its municipalities. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

28.name: Wildfires
28.note: Area burnt, not damage: land that burns twice counts twice.
28.description: Hectares burnt in each hex in the fires of 2016 to 2025 that the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS, Copernicus) mapped from satellite images: their perimeter, woodland or farmland, added up year by year (Spain: 1,284,332 ha in 7,303 fires). It records fires of about 30 ha or more (since 2021, with Sentinel-2, many smaller ones too); the smallest, which the ministry's statistic (EGIF) does count, are missing. It takes the place of the US map's FEMA disaster declarations. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

29.name: Great people
29.description: How many great people were born in each hex. 6,119 famous people born in today's Spain according to Wikidata, on the hex of their birthplace: Nobel laureates, kings and queens, conquistadors, navigators, soldiers, rebels, saints, philosophers, scientists, physicians, engineers, architects, painters, writers, film, singers, musicians, business people and athletes. Fame = the number of links to Wikipedias and other Wikimedia projects (sitelinks); each category keeps those who reach its threshold: nobel laureates 5, kings and queens 5, navigators and explorers 8, soldiers 10, rebels and guerrillas 5, saints and clergy 8, philosophers 8, scientists 8, physicians 5, inventors and engineers 5, architects 5, painters and sculptors 8, writers 10, film 15, singers 10, musicians and composers 10, business people and merchants 8, athletes 20; conquistadors, all of them. Someone in several categories goes in the first of this list. Left out: 344, of whom 180 were born outside today's Spain, 152 have only a country or a region as their birthplace and 12 have a birthplace without coordinates. Hover a hex to see who was born there, most famous first. Volunteer-edited: it reflects what Wikipedia covers, not a census. Colours span the 2nd–98th percentile of hexes; values beyond are drawn at the end colours.

30.name: Great people by trade
30.description: The category with the most people born in each hex (a tie goes to the first in the list); click one to show only that one. 6,119 famous people born in today's Spain according to Wikidata, on the hex of their birthplace: Nobel laureates, kings and queens, conquistadors, navigators, soldiers, rebels, saints, philosophers, scientists, physicians, engineers, architects, painters, writers, film, singers, musicians, business people and athletes. Fame = the number of links to Wikipedias and other Wikimedia projects (sitelinks); each category keeps those who reach its threshold: nobel laureates 5, kings and queens 5, navigators and explorers 8, soldiers 10, rebels and guerrillas 5, saints and clergy 8, philosophers 8, scientists 8, physicians 5, inventors and engineers 5, architects 5, painters and sculptors 8, writers 10, film 15, singers 10, musicians and composers 10, business people and merchants 8, athletes 20; conquistadors, all of them. Someone in several categories goes in the first of this list. Left out: 344, of whom 180 were born outside today's Spain, 152 have only a country or a region as their birthplace and 12 have a birthplace without coordinates. Hover a hex to see who was born there, most famous first. Volunteer-edited: it reflects what Wikipedia covers, not a census.
